cost_q1.title: How do you optimize your Serverless application's costs?
cost_q1.notes: Evidence: SDK clients created at module scope and reused; nothing bundled that the runtime/layer provides (package ~5 KB); Tracer patches only botocore (-14 ms init) - src/create_order/app.py L12-20. Log groups with 14-day retention for every function (template.yaml L400-404, L658-662, L693-697, L918-922). Cost-aware patterns: batch_writer for order lines, stream FilterCriteria so non-INSERT events never invoke the aggregator (template.yaml L645-648), analytics read pre-computed aggregates instead of scanning, GET /direct/orders skips Lambda entirely. Memory chosen with AWS Lambda Power Tuning (512 MB, balanced), arm64 for all functions (template.yaml L33-38, L104-106; README exercise 8).

ops_q1.title: How do you evaluate your Serverless application's health?
ops_q1.notes:
Evidence: X-Ray active tracing on API and functions with an orderId annotation (template.yaml L41, L307; src/create_order/app.py L109). Powertools JSON logs with request id, correlation id, cold-start flag and app_version (git SHA). Dashboard with API Gateway, Lambda, WAF, DLQ and IteratorAge widgets (template.yaml L818-916).
Gap (a1): there are NO CloudWatch alarms - out-of-the-box metrics are graphed but nobody is alerted on errors, throttles, 5XX, DLQ depth or IteratorAge.
Gap (a2): no application/business metrics (e.g. OrdersCreated, order value) - Powertools Metrics (EMF) is not used.

ops_q2.title: How do you approach application lifecycle management?
ops_q2.notes:
Evidence: everything is IaC (one SAM template) and deployed by GitHub Actions with OIDC; behaviour switches are template parameters (EnableCaching, PowertoolsLayerArn pinned, AppVersion = git SHA) with samconfig.toml config envs (a5).
Gap (a1/a4): one stage (prod) in one account - no separate dev/test environments or accounts; CI tests run, but deploys go straight to the only environment.
Gap (a2): no per-branch/temporary stacks (rebuild.sh recreates the same stack name).
Gap (a3): no gradual rollout - no AutoPublishAlias/DeploymentPreference (canary/linear) with alarm-based rollback; every deploy shifts 100% of traffic at once.
Gap (a6): runtime python3.12 - no tracked review of the Lambda runtime deprecation date.

perf_q1.title: How do you optimize your Serverless application's performance?
perf_q1.notes: Evidence: memory selected with Power Tuning (128-3008 MB, 50 invocations) - 512 MB was 38% faster than 256 MB (template.yaml L104-106). Direct API Gateway -> DynamoDB integration for reads, no Lambda (template.yaml L228-304). Cold start measured (scripts/measure_cold_start.sh) and init optimised (patch_modules, no bundled SDK; DAX client as a 1.4 MB --no-deps layer). Stream-based aggregation (batch 100, 5 s window) decouples analytics from the order write path (template.yaml L635-656). Caching: DAX read-through and API Gateway cache behind EnableCaching; analytics served from aggregates (README exercises 8-10, 13).

rel_q1.title: How do you regulate inbound request rates?
rel_q1.notes:
Evidence: API Gateway stage throttling 100 req/s, burst 50 on every method (template.yaml L315-337); WAF rate-based rule 100 requests / 5 min / IP returning 429 (template.yaml L791-806).
Gap (a3): no Lambda reserved concurrency - one noisy route could consume the account's concurrency and starve the other functions; the DAX cluster (single node when enabled) has no protection beyond the stage throttle.
Gap (a2): no usage plans / API keys / per-client quotas - all authenticated clients share the stage limit.

rel_q2.title: How do you build resiliency into your Serverless application?
rel_q2.notes:
Evidence (a1): stream consumer uses ReportBatchItemFailures, BisectBatchOnFunctionError, MaximumRetryAttempts 3 and an SQS on-failure destination (14-day retention, SSE) (template.yaml L610-656); batch_writer retries unprocessed items; whole payload validated before any write.
Evidence (a3): FilterCriteria drops non-INSERT events; the aggregator is exactly-once per record via a conditional EVENT#<eventID> marker in a transaction (src/analytics_aggregator/app.py; unit test redelivers a record).
Gap: POST /orders is NOT idempotent - a client retry after a timeout creates a second order (no idempotency key). Order lines are written with batch_writer, not a transaction, so a failure mid-way can leave a partial order.
Gap (a4): burst scaling not load tested.
N/A (a2): no long-running transactions in this workload.

not_applicable_choices.rel_rel_q2_a2: No long-running transactions - each request is a single short write or read.

sec_q1.title: How do you control access to your Serverless API?
sec_q1.notes: Evidence: Cognito user-pool authorizer is the DefaultAuthorizer for every route (template.yaml L308-314) - unauthenticated calls get 401 and never invoke Lambda (CI smoke test asserts 401). Regional endpoint with WAF web ACL and stage throttling. Access scoped by identity metadata: customerId comes from the verified sub claim (never the body); the direct integration filters by $context.authorizer.claims.sub so users only read their own orders (template.yaml L257-268); /analytics requires the Cognito group 'admins' (403 otherwise). Admin-only user creation, 12-char password policy, PreventUserExistenceErrors, 60-minute tokens (template.yaml L736-778).

sec_q2.title: How do you manage your Serverless application's security boundaries?
sec_q2.notes:
Evidence: Lambda resource policies are generated by SAM and scoped to this API's execute-api ARN; API Gateway's direct-integration role can only dynamodb:Query the Orders table (template.yaml L708-731). Temporary credentials everywhere between components: Lambda execution roles, API Gateway integration role, DAX service role, GitHub OIDC for CI (no stored keys). Four small single-purpose functions, each with its own role scoped to one table (CreateOrder can write but not read).
Gap (a2): network controls exist only for the DAX option (private subnets, security groups allowing 9111/443 from the Lambda SG only); otherwise WAF is the only network-layer control and it has only a rate rule.

sec_q3.title: How do you implement application Security in your workload?
sec_q3.notes:
Evidence (a4): the code uses no secrets - all AWS access via IAM roles; test-user passwords are random and written outside the repo (~/.orders-test-user.env); staged files are scanned for keys before commits. Evidence (a5): CreateOrder validates the whole payload (types, ranges, max 25 items, duplicates, finite non-negative prices) before writing (src/create_order/app.py L35-69); the VTL template escapes the path parameter ($util.escapeJavaScript) - injection attempt tested, returns 404.
Gap (a3): no automated dependency scanning (no Dependabot / Amazon Inspector for Lambda); Powertools layer and DAX client versions are pinned but updated manually.
Gap (a1/a2): no scheduled security-awareness review; no runtime protection.
